meta.titulo: Where Is Digital Sovereignty at Stake?
meta.descripcion: Master's thesis in Applied Ethics (UC) by Alejandro Bustos Núñez on authority and legitimacy in digital sovereignty, and the projects built around it.

institucion: Institute of Applied Ethics · Master's in Applied Ethics
titulo: Where Is Digital Sovereignty at Stake? Analyzing Authority and Legitimacy from a Technoethical Perspective

lineas: To Mom and Dad, here and in heaven
To the public education that formed me
For Ana, for her inspiration even from afar
And to Raúl, for the conversations and a profound acceptance

resumen: In this paper I ask what relationship with digital technical systems a democratic State needs in order to exercise legitimate authority over them. The dominant approaches to digital sovereignty, represented by Roberts (2024) and Fratini et al. (2024), give sovereignty a form without first shaping that relationship: they treat the norm as form and the technical system as matter. Drawing on Gilbert Simondon's critique of the hylomorphic scheme, I argue that jurisdictional, acquisition and implementation instruments are part of the associated milieu of the systems they aim to govern, and that they readjust to those systems when the State merely conditions what someone else anticipated. I propose the criterion of high technicity: a State exercises digital sovereignty when it takes part in the individuation of those systems with technical culture and retains the capacity to re-individuate with them. With Philip Pettit, I link that criterion to legitimacy: the State is legitimate when it neither dominates nor allows domination of the community that inhabits the system's associated milieu. I illustrate the framework with the case of Google's data center in Cerrillos.
nota: This work is carried out under the guidance of Gabriela Arriagada Bruneau. I am a thesis student in FONDECYT Regular project No. 1261259 “Knowledge, power and subjectivation in the age of algorithmic technologies of government”.

proyectos.titulo: What is being built around it
proyectos.intro: The thesis is about a State. While writing it I kept starting other projects, some in direct consonance with it and others more peripheral, that ask the same question from the community and from practice: what does it mean to take part in the individuation of the systems that govern us?

cooperativa.bajada: A cooperative whose members host their own infrastructure and receive a Solid pod with an open identity (WebID). It is the inverse of Cerrillos: the community anticipates its own associated milieu.

software.bajada: espacio and a set of small apps that separate data from the application, so anyone can replace or abandon an app without losing what is theirs.

arquitecturas.bajada: Architecture notes on Solid and Linked Data: another way of coupling system and milieu, with infrastructure distributed across homes instead of hyperscale data centers.

estetica.bajada: An ethics that emerges in individuation, instead of applying norms to given objects. I cut it from the thesis text for length.

audioteca.bajada: Narrated audio with open voices: a podcast on Simondon's Individuation and another that unfolds the thesis argument.

cuentos.bajada: Sael: speculative fiction about a digital technician in a society organized in mesh networks after a crisis.

criterios.intro: Six questions I propose in the thesis to tell whether a State, or a community, takes part in the genesis of a technical system or only readjusts to it. Pick a case, move the values and compare the shapes. Cerrillos is the thesis case; the others are hypothetical and small-scale.

ui.radar: Radar chart of the six criteria of high technicity
ui.nota: The values are my own reading, meant for thinking with. They are not a measurement.

ejes.pregunta: Does the system build local capacities?
Does the local milieu change any design decision of the system?
When the milieu changes, does the system readjust or does the milieu?
Can the operation be reversed without the service collapsing?
Can the State read the system, or only sanction it?
Who in the community of the associated milieu had a voice? Who was excluded?

cerrillos.resumen: High technicity appeared scattered and through conflict. The collective learned to read the system and forced the shift to air cooling, but Google defined how the readjustment happened and the formal channels excluded the collective.

mesh.resumen: A neighborhood builds and maintains its own antenna network with open firmware. Neighbors understand the system because they set it up, change it when the milieu changes and can disconnect it without the neighborhood collapsing.

liceo.nombre: High school with a proprietary school platform
liceo.resumen: A school contracts a cloud platform with no access to the code or to exportable data. The vendor defines the design, the school only readjusts, and leaving the platform would cost a year of teachers' work.

municipio.nombre: Municipality with a free-software permit desk
municipio.resumen: A town's IT team migrates its permit desk to free software and runs open workshops to read the code. It gains the ability to read and to change the system, but residents do not yet take part in design decisions.

agua.nombre: Rural water committee with open sensors
agua.resumen: A rural drinking-water committee installs open-design moisture sensors and keeps the data in its own pod. Neighbors took part from the first prototype, though the committee depends on a single technician.

consultorio.nombre: Clinic with a single-vendor medical record
consultorio.resumen: A clinic uses a medical record system whose format cannot be exported. Staff can operate it but not read it, and changing vendors would mean retyping years of patient histories.
